findings.description: The function iterates over the `records` iterable twice: first to compute the `total` sum (line 2) and second to construct the dictionary (line 3). If `records` is a one-shot iterator (e.g., a generator), the second iteration will find the iterator exhausted, resulting in an empty dictionary being returned regardless of the input content.

review.summary: The implementation consumes the `records` iterator when calculating `total`, making it empty for the dictionary comprehension. This violates the requirement to support one-shot iterators.
